item.title: Ogun approves N50,000 welfare palliative for 3,050 corps members
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State government has approved a welfare palliative of ₦50,000 each for the 3,050 members of the 2026 Batch C, Stream I of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) currently undergoing their orientation programme at the NYSC camp in Sagamu. The intervention, approved by the administration of Governor Dapo Abiodun, is part of the government’s ongoing efforts to ease the burden of prevailing economic challenges on young Nigerians and provide support for corps members serving in the state. This was contained in a statement signed by the State Commissioner for Sports Development, Wasiu Isiaka, and made available to newsmen in Abeokuta. According to the statement, the disbursement of the funds commenced on Monday, with each eligible corps member to receive ₦50,000 to help meet personal and other essential needs during the orientation period. It reads, “The initiative underscores the state government’s recognition of the contributions of corps members to national development and its commitment to promoting their welfare, comfort and overall well-being throughout their service year. “The government acknowledges that corps members, many of whom are away from their families and familiar environments, face various financial and personal demands as they settle into their new assignments. The additional financial support is intended to provide some relief and make their transition into the service year more manageable. “Beyond the financial palliative, the state government has also approved the donation of 500 mattresses to the NYSC orientation camp in Sagamu to strengthen the camp’s capacity to accommodate corps members comfortably. “The intervention comes amid an increase in the number of corps members deployed to Ogun State, making continuous investment in camp facilities and essential amenities necessary to sustain appropriate living conditions for participants. “The provision of mattresses forms part of the government’s broader commitment to supporting the NYSC programme and ensuring that corps members have access to decent accommodation and a conducive environment during their orientation exercise. “The state government, therefore, considers their welfare an important aspect of creating a supportive environment in which they can discharge their responsibilities effectively and have a rewarding service year.” The government also encourages corps members to embrace the values of discipline, patriotism, tolerance and selfless service, and to take full advantage of the opportunities provided by the NYSC scheme to contribute meaningfully to their host communities and the country at large. item.title: How To Protect Yourself From Ebola Infection
item.description: The Federal Government on Tuesday confirmed the first case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Ebola is a disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person or animal, according to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). ﻿ Following the confirmation, below are facts on transmission/causes, symptoms, and how to protect yourself and loved ones. How Does It Spread? Ebola can be spread through: Direct contact with blood, sweat, saliva, vomit, or other bodily fluids of an infected, symptomatic person Touching contaminated surfaces such as clothing, bedding, or other materials contaminated with fluids from an infected individual Consuming infected wild animals, handling deceased bodies without safety gear. Know The Symptoms Symptoms typically appear two to 21 days after exposure. The symptoms include: Fever Vomitting Headache Diarrhea Weakness/Fatigue Bleeding Muscle pain Sore throat How To Protect Yourself Wash hands regularly with clean running water and soap, or use alcohol-based sanitiser. Avoid contact with dead bodies and wild animals. Ensure all meat products are handled hygienically and thoroughly cooked. Do not touch bodily fluids of sick individuals or handle deceased bodies without professional health protocols. Health workers should adhere strictly to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) standards. Myth Vs Facts Let’s set the record straight! Myth: Ebola spreads via casual contact (handshake, hugging). Fact: Ebola does not spread through casual contact. It requires direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person. Myth: Ebola spreads through food and water. Fact: Ebola does not spread through food and water, but all foods should be thoroughly cooked. Drink water always. Myth: Ebola spreads through the air. Fact: Ebola is not an airborne virus. Transmission strictly requires direct physical contact with bodily fluids or contaminated objects from a person showing active symptoms. Myth: Healthcare facilities are not safe during outbreaks. Fact: Healthcare facilities are strengthening infection prevention and control measures, including triage systems, hand hygiene, use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and isolation procedures to protect patients and healthcare workers. Stay informed and avoid panic. Spreading unverified rumours causes unnecessary fear and hampers response efforts. Always rely on official health updates. item.description: Delayed diagnosis and a dearth of essential medical resources continue to hinder Nigeria’s public health response more than the nature of the Ebola virus, a professor at the College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Dr. Alero Roberts, has said. ﻿ Roberts explained that the pathogen’s behaviour remains unchanged and predictable, adding that the real problem lies in systemic shortcomings and hesitation by members of the public, which she said compromises patient outcomes before medical intervention can begin. “I have no problem with the virus itself; the virus is doing what the virus does, it hasn’t changed its behaviour, and the virus is doing what the virus does,.” she said during an interview on Channel Television’s The Morning Brief on Wednesday, while reacting to Nigeria’s first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain of he virus. “We do have problems with the delayed diagnosis, seeking appropriate care and definitely with the availability of resources to cope.” The doctor also noted that no country in the world has the resources to manage the massive outbreak of the virus. “No country in the world today has the resources to cope with the massive outbreak of Ebola. Once the diagnosis has been made, Ebola becomes a nursing care issue, and there are just not enough nurses; kudos to the nurses, there are just not enough nurses to cope with the major outbreak of Ebola,” Roberts said. “Which is what we are seeing in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) already, so we must stick with prevention, border control, identifying, and as a public health physician I will be going with high index of suspicion to treat every patient as a possible case and initiate what we call the IPC ring. “The IPC ring is Infection Prevention and Control; we have got to initiate that because those are our first line of defense and they have proven very effective in the past,” she added. item.title: Macron Lands In Saudi Arabia On Surprise ‘Solidarity’ Visit
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron landed in Riyadh, where he is due to meet Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Wednesday, in a surprise “solidarity” visit after weeks of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Macron is the first Western leader to visit the kingdom since Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis intensified their attacks this month. The trip is part of a Gulf tour to secure diesel and petrol supplies as Macron seeks to bring down energy prices following violent protests in France sparked by rising living costs that have created a political crisis for the president. “The president of the republic is travelling to Saudi Arabia this afternoon to meet with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman,” a statement from Macron’s office said. The visit aimed to “demonstrate France’s solidarity with the kingdom in the face of the attacks carried out by the Houthis against its territory, and to continue efforts undertaken on securing and diversifying hydrocarbon supplies”, it added. France’s President Emmanuel Macron, flanked by Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani (L) and Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, attends the 9th Annual One Planet Sovereign Wealth Funds (OPSWF) Summit at the Rosewood Hotel in Lusail on October 21, 2026. In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh airport to shut and the postponement of a major investment conference. A Houthi attempt to blockade Saudi ports is also hampering oil exports from the kingdom. item.title: Barca’s Olmo injured for a month, misses Clasico
item.description: Barcelona midfielder Dani Olmo will miss Sunday’s Clasico in La Liga against Real Madrid after being ruled out for around a month through injury on Wednesday. “Tests have confirmed that Dani Olmo is suffering an injury to his left thigh,” said Spanish champions Barcelona in a statement, confirming he will be sidelined for “approximately one month”. The Spain international went off hurt during Barca’s 4-2 Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday in the French capital. As well as the visit of Real Madrid to Camp Nou, Olmo is set to miss league games against Alaves and Atletico Madrid, as well as facing Aston Villa in the Champions League. Olmo will also likely be unable to play for World Cup winners Spain in Nations League games against the Czech Republic and England on November 12 and 15 respectively. The 28-year-old, who joined Barca from RB Leipzig in 2024, has suffered frequently with injuries through his career. item.title: Presidential Election: Tinubu got 517,341 Kano votes in 2023; can he win it in 2027?
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor Ahead of the 2027 presidential poll, all eyes, including that of President Bola Tinubu, are on Kano, the commercial nerve centre of northern Nigeria. Read Also: * Kano gov assures Tinubu of Northern support for 2027 * 2027: APC chairman predicts 70% North’s votes for Tinubu * 2027: Atiku will win Kano without Kwankwaso, ADC campaign declares As in the past, President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC; Alhaji Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, ADC; and Mr Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, are locked in an intense battle for Kano votes. In the 2023 presidential election, the state was won by Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria People s Party, NNPP. He scored 997,279 votes to floor Tinubu, who came second with 517,341votes. Atiku Abubakar, who ran on the platform of the People’s Democratic Party, PDP, got 131,716 votes. Obi of the Labour Party, LP, polled28,513 votes. 2027 Presidential Election: Same candidates, different dynamics Four years down the line, some factors have changed even though all the contestants are in the race. Now, Kwankwaso is running as vice presidential candidate to Peter Obi. He is not the main flag bearer. Will Kano voters give him the kind of support they gave him in the past now that he is no longer the presidential candidate? On the other hand, will they swing their support for Atiku, a fellow northerner who is now running on ADC platform? Or will the Kano voters give their support to President Bola Tinubu, who is still running on the plank of the ruling APC and ensure he secures more than the 517,341 votes he got four years ago? These are questions that will be answered in 86 days time. item.title: Ebola: Senate urges FG to make screening mandatory at all entry points

The motion came on the heels of a report that Nigeria has recorded a case of Ebola in a female patient who travelled from Uganda in East Africa to Abuja, capital of the West African state. item.title: 2027: Sowore’s AAC writes Tinubu, demands presidential villa for campaign council inauguration
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba The African Action Congress (AAC) has formally requested approval from President Bola Tinubu to hold the inauguration of its Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa in Aso Rock, Abuja, and has asked for logistical support for 5,000 participants. In a letter dated 21 October 2026 and signed by National Secretary Oshiokhue Philip Ikpeminoghena, the party said it wants to stage the ceremony on 11 November 2026 “in preparation for the 2027 general elections.” The AAC also requested the provision of food, drinks and other logistical support for the 5,000 expected attendees from within Nigeria and abroad. The party said the request was made “consistent with the arrangements reportedly extended to the All Progressives Congress (APC) for a similar political engagement.” “In the spirit of multiparty democracy, political inclusiveness, and equal treatment of political parties,” the letter stated, granting the request would demonstrate the Presidency’s commitment to fairness, equal access, and the principle that public institutions must serve all Nigerians without partisan discrimination. The AAC said it looks forward to a favourable response and asked for information on the applicable procedures and conditions for approval. The letter was addressed to the President and Commander-in-Chief at the Presidential Villa, Aso Rock, Abuja. item.title: Netanyahu’s main election rival rules out serving under him
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival in October 27 elections, ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Wednesday that he would refuse to serve as a minister in a new government led by the current premier. With the poll just days away, and predictions that no side will win on its own, some commentators have raised the possibility of a unity government convening Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc with centrist and centre-right parties. But speaking to radio station 103 FM on Wednesday, Eisenkot said he was committed, “categorically, to not serving under Netanyahu’s leadership, even within the framework of a rotation” deal in which the two shared power. Eisenkot has campaigned on attacking the fitness to serve of Netanyahu, especially over his failure to prevent the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Polls show Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition and the opposition camp rallying around Eisenkot are neck and neck, with each projected to win around 50 to 52 seats — just shy of a majority in the 120-member Knesset. In his interview, Eisenkot did not rule out the possibility of a unity government altogether. Former prime minister Naftali Bennet, whose party is polling third, said a government that included the current prime minister would not be an issue for him. It would, however, run counter to Israeli law, which forbids anyone facing charges from serving as a minister — although the bar does not apply for prime minister. Netanyahu is currently on trial and faces several charges of corruption, which he denies. An October 16 poll found that 55 percent of respondents would prefer a unity government over new elections should the upcoming vote fail to produce a clear winner. In 2020, Netanyahu and centrist Benny Gantz set aside their mutual antipathy to strike a power-sharing deal in which they would rotate the prime ministership between them. The agreement followed a period that saw three elections in less than a year, and the resulting government lasted only 13 months. item.title: Delta youths seize Macaraba oil field over alleged marginalization
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume Hundreds of youths from Ifie-Kporo community in Warri South local government area of Delta state yesterday (today Wednesday) shut down operations at the Macaraba oil field, accusing the operating firm of marginalising the community and refusing to recognise it as a host community. The protesters, who arrived at the field in speedboats, demanded justice, youth employment, and recognition of the community’s rights over Wells 24 and 25. They carried placards with several inscriptions which included , “We Want Justice,” “Employ Our Youths,” and “Give Us Our Rights or Leave Our Land.” The youths accused the oil firm of operating on their ancestral land without adequately recognising or engaging the community, vowing to remain at the field until their grievances are addressed. Speaking during the protest, one of the youths, who gave his name as Tosan, said the company had been unfair to the community and warned that the occupation would continue until their demands were met. The protesters insisted that Wells 24 and 25 sit on Ifie-Kporo ancestral land and urged the firm to respect their rights as a host community in line with the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA). They called on the company to follow the precedent set by Gulf, which they said had recognised and engaged with the community as host to its oil facilities. The youths warned that continued neglect of their demands could threaten peace in the area, and urged the firm to resolve the dispute through dialogue rather than allow the situation to escalate. item.title: 5 things to know about Chinese AI startup DeepSeek
item.description: The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China. Here are five things to know about the Chinese AI startup following the new restrictions: – ‘Sputnik moment’ – Founded by Liang Wenfeng in the eastern Chinese tech hub Hangzhou, DeepSeek started life in 2023 as a side project of Liang’s data-driven hedge fund that had access to a cache of powerful AI processors made by US chip giant Nvidia. It gained global attention in January 2025 with the release of its R1 deep-reasoning large language model, which sparked a US tech share sell-off. Industry insiders were stunned by R1’s high performance — at a level similar to ChatGPT and other leading US chatbots — and DeepSeek’s claims to have developed it at a fraction of the cost. Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen described it as a “Sputnik moment”, referencing the 1957 launch of Earth’s first artificial satellite by the Soviet Union that stunned the Western world. – Censorship concerns – Like other Chinese chatbots, DeepSeek’s AI tools eschew topics usually censored in the world’s second-largest economy, such as the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. That and data privacy concerns have led DeepSeek AI to be banned or restricted on government-issued devices in several countries, including the United States, Australia and South Korea. On Monday, the US went further by banning civilian government agencies from using products developed by DeepSeek and third-party tools created using DeepSeek. China’s foreign ministry said it opposed that move and accused the US of “overstretching” the concept of national security. item.title: Toulouse v Troyes Ligue 1 game postponed as France gripped by unrest
item.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has has pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. item.title: Jonathan urges Nigeria to shift from imports to production
item.description: By Soni Daniel ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria to develop the resources and technology needed to produce goods and services locally rather than continue to depend on imports. Jonathan made the call on Wednesday while commissioning the Zeetin Technologies plant in Idu, Abuja, which manufactures tricycles for the Nigerian market. He said Nigeria’s large youth population could serve as a major asset in boosting local production, creating economic opportunities and driving national development. The former president urged Nigeria to emulate countries that had successfully mobilised their resources and young populations to expand their manufacturing capacity and become reliable producers and exporters of goods. He stressed the need for Nigeria to harness its human and material resources to strengthen domestic production and reduce dependence on imported goods. item.title: Toluwanisings’ family announces service of songs, seeks support for widow, children
item.description: The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has announced a night of tributes and service of songs in his honour while appealing to the public for financial support for his wife and children. The event is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 3pm at the Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, Ibadan, Oyo State. The family announced the programme in a post on the singer’s social media page, inviting friends, colleagues, fans and well-wishers to celebrate his life and ministry. “We invite you to join us for a Night of Tributes and Service of Songs in honour of our beloved brother, friend, and gospel minister, Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, fondly known as Toluwanisings,” the statement read. In a separate appeal titled “A Call for Love and Support,” the family urged Nigerians to assist the singer’s wife and children following his death on October 14. The family called on well-meaning individuals to contribute towards supporting the widow as she navigates life after the loss of her husband. “As we mourn the loss of our beloved brother, let us stand with his wife during this difficult season. Every contribution, no matter how small, is a gesture of love and compassion,” the family said. It also provided account details for donations and prayed for blessings on those willing to support the bereaved family. “Please support her through the account details provided. May God bless every giving heart and grant the family strength and comfort,” the statement added. Toluwanisings died on October 14, 2026, hours after ministering at a praise concert organised by fellow gospel singer Bidemi Olaoba in Ibadan. His death sparked widespread reactions on social media, with questions raised about access to emergency medical care after his personal assistant alleged that several hospitals refused to admit him. The planned night of tributes and service of songs will provide an opportunity for family members, friends, colleagues and fans to honour the late singer’s life and musical contributions. Coker also cautioned against rumours, discrimination and stigmatisation, urging residents to share only information from verified public health sources. She said the Ogun State Government would continue to work with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and other relevant partners to monitor developments and implement appropriate measures to protect public health. item.title: Suspected kidnappers kill 7-year-old boy hours after demanding N2.5m ransom in Jos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos A seven-year-old boy, Abdullahi Rabi’u, has been found dead hours after suspected kidnappers abducted him and demanded a ransom of N2.5 million in Majema area, along Ring Road, Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victim’s uncle, Sukairaj Danladi Gado, who narrated the incident, said the boy was sent on an errand to a neighbour’s house on Monday evening but failed to return after delivering the message. “The family became worried when Abdullahi did not return home. We made efforts to locate him, but all our efforts proved abortive,” Gado said. He said, “On Tuesday morning, we received a call from an unidentified telephone number. The caller demanded N2.5 million as ransom and informed us that the boy had been kidnapped.” According to him, “We agreed to pay the ransom because we wanted the boy to return home alive. We were hoping that he would be released, but what happened later shattered our hopes.” Gado said, “We were devastated when we received the news that his body had been found. It was a painful experience for the family because we had hoped to secure his release.” He added, “The boy’s body was reportedly discovered on Tuesday evening in a narrow passage near his family’s residence. The incident has thrown the family and residents of the neighbourhood into mourning.” Expressing concern over the killing, the uncle said, “We suspect that the people behind this incident may be familiar with the neighbourhood. We want security agencies to investigate the matter and ensure that those responsible are arrested.” He further said, “We are appealing to the security agencies to do everything possible to unravel the circumstances surrounding his death and bring the perpetrators to justice so that other families will not experience this kind of tragedy.” Efforts to obtain reactions from security operatives were unsuccessful as of press time. item.title: Ebola: Senate Seeks Emergency Funding, Mandatory Screening At All Entry Points
item.description: The Senate has called on the Federal Government to provide emergency funding from the service-wide vote to strengthen the country’s disease surveillance system and enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. The resolution followed a motion of urgent national importance sponsored by Senator Francis Faduyile, who raised concerns over the spread of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus and the risk it poses to Nigeria’s public health system. Faduyile noted that the outbreak, which began in the DRC, had spread to other African countries, including Uganda and Kenya, highlighting the risk of infected travellers entering Nigeria through third countries. He also cited the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention’s assessment of a high risk of Ebola importation, recalling that a single traveller brought the disease into Nigeria through Lagos in July 2014. ﻿ The Senate acknowledged the Federal Government’s existing measures, including the introduction of health declaration forms and enhanced screening at entry points. However, it expressed concern that screening requirements had been restricted to travellers from selected countries, potentially leaving gaps in the country’s surveillance system. Lawmakers also raised concerns over inadequate staffing and equipment at several entry points, as well as the continued reliance of Port Health Services on the Quarantine Act of 1926. item.title: 2027: Court dismisses suit seeking registration of new political party
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed a suit seeking to compel Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to register a political association as Wisdom Party (WP), 88 days to the 2027 presidential election. Justice James Omotosho, in a judgment, held that the plaintiff’s claim lacked merit and the suit had become academic. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the plaintiff, Chief Mrs Chinasa Nwekeke, had filed the suit as the pro tem National Chairman and on behalf of Wisdom Party, a political association seeking a registration as a party. Nwekeke, in the originating summons marked FHC//ABJ/CS/746/2026 filed on April 14 by her lawyer, Mark Agbo, had sued INEC as the sole defendant. item.content:encoded: The Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed a suit seeking to compel Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to register a political association as Wisdom Party (WP), 88 days to the 2027 presidential election. Justice James Omotosho, in a judgment, held that the plaintiff’s claim lacked merit and the suit had become academic. Nwekeke, in the originating summons marked FHC//ABJ/CS/746/2026 filed on April 14 by her lawyer, Mark Agbo, had sued INEC as the sole defendant. She also sought a declaration that the provision of Section 75 (6) of the Electoral Act, 2022, which provides for a separate source of funds in the form of a fee or levy on political associations for the performance of the constitutional function of registration of political parties, is inconsistent with Section 4 (1) (f) of the Electoral Act, 2022, and thus should be struck down by the court. Nwekeke further submitted that INEC’s failure in providing its account details to the plaintiff’s association for payment of the administrative fee was deemed to be a waiver and that it was meant to frustrate the application of the plaintiff’s association. The electoral umpire, in its counter affidavit, stated that the plaintiff’s letter of intent did not have a symbol of the party and that the general election is fixed for January 2027, which means that the court, granting the reliefs of the plaintiff, means that it would be required to file a formal application letter and it would be less than 12 months to the general election. The commission also submitted that the letter of intent written by the plaintiff’s association did not meet the requirements of the law, as it did not contain the symbol of the proposed political party, and thus it is void. It argued that since there was no valid letter of intent, the plaintiff’s association had no right to claim reliefs. INEC, therefore, urged the court to refuse the reliefs sought. Delivering the judgment, Justice Omotosho observed that from a cursory look at Section 3, especially Section 3 (2)(c), aids, grants or any other accruals are quite open-ended. “An accrual in accounting terms refers to revenues and expenses. “This means that revenues generated by the defendant can be paid into the Independent National Electoral Commission Fund. “The administrative fee being debated by the plaintiff is meant for the registration of political parties, and being a revenue accruing to the defendant, it can rightly be paid into the Fund. “Importantly, this also implies that the defendant is within its powers to demand administrative or processing fees, such as fees for the production and certification of the national voters register. “The fact that an institution receives funding from the Federation Account does not mean that it cannot generate funds or charge fees for some of its activities. “For instance, the judiciary receives funding from the Consolidated Revenue Fund; however, courts still fix filing fees and processing fees for court processes. “There is no express prohibition on the defendant to refrain from fixing administrative fees. “Consequently, I hold that the defendant has powers to fix administrative fees for the purpose of registration of political parties. “In final analysis, the claim of the plaintiff is without merit, and the suit has become academic. item.title: Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France
item.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has been pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match, which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday, will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday, with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. PSG will host Lyon at the same venue in a Ligue 1 match on Sunday evening. AFP The post Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Cross River State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, endorsing the proposed establishment of state police to address insecurity through a decentralised policing system. All 22 lawmakers present at plenary voted in favour of the bill, with none opposing it. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. Ayambem, however, stressed that the implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, said policing must be brought closer to the people. He argued that a decentralised system would improve security responses and enable law enforcement agencies to address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies to ensure that the proposed State Police Services complemented existing security structures and improved overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, emphasised the need for adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism in the proposed system. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect citizens’ fundamental rights. Lawmakers also identified improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as potential benefits of decentralised policing. The passage marks the Cross River Assembly’s endorsement of the proposed constitutional amendments. The bill must proceed through the constitutionally prescribed amendment process before the proposed changes can take effect nationally. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. His arrival triggered an emergency response involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Lagos State Government, the NCDC and international health partners. According to a report published in the United States Centres for Disease Control and Prevention’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases, comprising 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, by September 24, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014.
